business_problem: Global financial services company BNY Mellon houses and manages critical data for its clients and wanted to incorporate flexibility and resiliency into one of its self-managed databases. The company sought a solution built around tailored microservices to support its cloud-native data management offering.
solution_summary: Global financial services company BNY Mellon houses and manages critical data for its clients and wanted to incorporate flexibility and resiliency into one of its self-managed databases. The company sought a solution built around tailored microservices to support its cloud-native data management offering. BNY Mellon turned to Microsoft Azure, and within nine months, it migrated to Azure Database for PostgreSQL and created a cohesive, customized solution. The company’s simplified data storage and analytics capability enhances how it helps clients turn data into meaningful insights. The transition has also given BNY Mellon employees more time to focus on innovation as the company seeks new ways to serve clients with technology. BNY Mellon is a global financial services firm that helps its customers invest and service their financial assets and manages large quantities of critical data on their behalf.

solution_components.name: Azure Database for PostgreSQL
solution_components.role: Provides a managed database layer for resilient, scalable operational data workloads.

evidence_quotes: Global financial services company BNY Mellon houses and manages critical data for its clients and wanted to incorporate flexibility and resiliency into one of its self-managed databases.
The company sought a solution built around tailored microservices to support its cloud-native data management offering.

An important component of the company’s cloud-native Data Vault data management solution, a self-managed database environment, was less efficient than it could be, and the company wanted to invest in new technology to enhance its reliability and agility.
“Our services must be highly resilient to meet the scale and availability of our multitenant architecture.”

“Our clients are trusting us with their data, and as a leading data management platform for asset and wealth managers, asset owners, and market infrastructure players, it’s imperative that our technology is resilient and scalable to support their growth in new regions and asset classes while making information more actionable to users,” says Steve Taylor, Head of Product for Data and Analytics at BNY Mellon.

The team at BNY Mellon wanted to improve and simplify its self-managed database environment with a fully managed and more efficient, flexible, and resilient database technology that would better fit its microservices architecture.
